title: Git-to-tracker drift detector in doctor
description: Context: a 2h47m dabble-employee-app agent session made 300 CLI calls with 24 failures. Failure clusters: 117 read-only work show polls (~40% of all calls), 14 identical failed sync refresh retries, 6 vault init retries, 66 agent finish calls with only 2 standalone evidence records, 6 NOT_FOUND finish/release (ownership confusion), 1 CONFLICT claim, 2 POLICY_VIOLATION sprint closes. Design principle for this mission: every response (success or error) must carry enough state that the correct next action is derivable without another read, and the honest path (evidence, ownership, health) must be the path of least resistance. Problem: in the audited project, six findings worth of commits landed while the tracker still showed the tasks as ready — drift was only caught by a human eyeballing git log against work list. Change: doctor scans recent commits on the current branch for work-ID references (the bw_work_ id pattern, plus configurable patterns) and cross-checks referenced items status; commits referencing open work older than a threshold produce a drift finding listing the work IDs and commit SHAs. Where: doctor implementation; git log parsing can follow the patterns in docs/architecture/GIT_HEALTH_HARDENING.md. Constraint: read-only finding, never auto-closes work; must be cheap (bounded commit window, default ~50 commits); silent when the repo has no work-ID references at all.
acceptanceCriteria: doctor flags commits referencing still-open work items with both the work ID and the commit SHA
Detector is read-only, bounded to a configurable recent-commit window, and silent when no references exist
